proof.text: Both $v_!$ and $v^*$ are additive exact functors on constant-$A$ module sheaves: use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] for sum extension and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] for inverse image, including its identification with ringed-topos module pullback. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], applying either functor degreewise represents its functor on the entire unbounded derived category and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. In particular the $v_!$ in this proof is sum extension, not a compactification-dependent candidate for compact supports.

Represent $B$ and $M$ by complexes and choose quasi-isomorphisms $P\to B$ and $Q\to M$ with $P,Q$ K-flat and with flat terms, by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the two constant ringed sites. Here and below an arrow to a derived object abbreviates an arrow to its chosen complex representative. The preservation clause in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives that $v^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms; exactness in step 1 identifies its derived pullback with $v^*B$. By [lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat], $v_!Q$ is also K-flat with flat terms. All hypotheses hold: $v$ is separated etale of finite type and the coefficient sheaves are constant; the cited results impose no boundedness or constructibility condition.

proof.text:
Write $\beta$ for signed tensor symmetry: in bidegree $(p,q)$ it sends $b\otimes m$ to $(-1)^{pq}m\otimes b$. From the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], its two differential terms have signs $(-1)^{(p+1)q}$ and $(-1)^{p+p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}$, respectively, agreeing with the differential after symmetry; hence it is a chain isomorphism. Apply [lem-pur-etale-sum-tensor-totalization] to $(Q,P)$. The composite
$$v_!\operatorname{Tot}(v^*P\otimes Q)\xrightarrow{v_!\beta}v_!\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes v^*P)\xrightarrow{\Psi_{Q,P}^{-1}}\operatorname{Tot}(v_!Q\otimes P)\xrightarrow{\beta}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes v_!Q)$$
is a natural chain isomorphism $\pi_{P,Q}$. The two symmetry signs are both $(-1)^{pq}$ and cancel. Consequently its inverse sends the lift-indexed generator $b\otimes(s,m)$ to $(s,s^*b\otimes m)$, with no sign. This follows directly from the component formula for $\Psi$ in the cited statement. It uses direct-sum totalizations even in an unbounded total degree.

proof.text: The model comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], together with step 2, identifies the two localizations in step 3 with $v_!(v^*B\otimes_A^L M)$ and $B\otimes_A^L v_!M$. This is the derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Thus $\pi_{P,Q}$ represents the comparison specified in the item: its inverse is exactly the termwise sum-extension pure-tensor map, with the tensor factors in the stated order. Its naturality on homotopy categories is supplied by the totalization statement in step 3. To descend in both variables, use separately the equivalence from the localization of flat-term K-flat complexes to $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and to $D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For each fixed first variable, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends the natural transformation in the second variable. Descend its naturality in the first variable by the same clause; uniqueness, clause (3), preserves these naturality equations. Apply the same process to $\pi^{-1}$; the inverse equations descend by clause (3). This gives the specified natural isomorphism $P_{B,M}$, independently of resolutions, on the two entire derived categories.

proof.text: Here is the counit normalization needed for the equality. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], an etale test object $(W,s)$ over $V$ identifies $(v^*H)(W,s)$ with $H(W)$; the comparison is $A$-linear because [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] transports the action through the constant-ring comparison. On the presheaf defining $v_!v^*H$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], send the summand element $(s,h)$ to $h\in H(W)$ and add over finitely supported summands. This is compatible with restrictions and $A$-linear, so factors uniquely through sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. This fold is the counit: maps from the sum presheaf to $H$ are precisely restriction-compatible families of maps into $H(W)$, hence maps into $v^*H$; the displayed fold corresponds to $1_{v^*H}$. This identifies the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] its complex counit is degreewise this fold, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends it with its triangle identities. It is therefore the fold counit $\epsilon$ of the termwise adjunction in the item.

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P,R$ of $B,C$ as in step 2. By [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes R)$ is itself flat-term K-flat. The current statement of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] includes the ordinary comparison, its pure-tensor formula and inverse, together with coefficient-change and quotient-transition equations; the ordinary clause gives the chain map sending $s^*b\otimes s^*c$ to $s^*(b\otimes c)$. On these K-flat models it represents the canonical $\theta$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. We check the required identity before localization, after precomposing with $\pi_{P,v^*R}^{-1}$. On the $(p,q)$ summand, take $b\in P^p(W)$ and $c\in R^q(W)$ in the summand indexed by a lift $s:W\to V$. By steps 3 and 5, the left composite sends $b\otimes(s,c)$ to $b\otimes c$. The right composite sends it successively to $(s,s^*b\otimes s^*c)$, then to $(s,s^*(b\otimes c))$ under $v_!\theta$, and finally to $b\otimes c$ under the fold. There are no signs: no tensor factors are permuted in these composites. Equality on these generators gives equality of sheaf maps by the tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Equality on every summand gives equality in each total degree; the direct-sum compatibility in [lem-pur-etale-sum-tensor-totalization] identifies those degree maps with the displayed complex composites. Since $\pi^{-1}$ is invertible, this proves the desired equality of chain maps on these representatives.

proof.text:
Localize the equality of step 6. Steps 4 and 5 identify its terms with $P_{B,v^*C}$ and the specified derived counits, while the pullback comparison in step 6 is the canonical $\theta_{B,C}$. Therefore it reads
$$(1_B\otimes\epsilon_C)\circ P_{B,v^*C}=\epsilon_{B\otimes_A^LC}\circ v_!(\theta_{B,C}).$$
Every $B,C$ has the flat-term K-flat representatives used above by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The bifunctorial descent and detection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes this equality independent of representatives and valid for arbitrary derived morphisms. No boundedness or finite Tor amplitude was used, so both the isomorphism and its counit compatibility hold for all unbounded $B,M,C$.

title: Tensor compatibility for etale sum extension
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $v:V\to T$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes (schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings). On the entire ordinary etale derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves, for $B\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the canonical map induced by the termwise sum-extension construction
$$v_!(v^*B\otimes_A^L M)\longrightarrow B\otimes_A^L v_!M$$
is an isomorphism. Write $P_{B,M}$ for this comparison and $\epsilon_C:v_!v^*C\to C$ for the fold counit of $v_!\dashv v^*$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. For every $C\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ its counit compatibility is the identity
$$(1_B\otimes\epsilon_C)\circ P_{B,v^*C}=\epsilon_{B\otimes_A^LC}\circ v_!(\theta_{B,C}),$$
where $\theta_{B,C}:v^*B\otimes_A^Lv^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*(B\otimes_A^LC)$ is the canonical tensor-pullback comparison. The assertion and this equality hold for arbitrary unbounded $B,M,C$. The notation and functors used here are the ones in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] [def-kun-derived-tensor] [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The scheme, Noetherian, etale, separated and finite-type notions are as in [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
